reports.lens: Stage map: every step of one T9 blog piece, from angle to approved/held, with the LLM calls, the F-gates, the attempt loop and the worst-case number of calls

findings.claim: The loop allows at most 3 attempts per piece (MAX_ATTEMPTS=3). Attempt 1 is a fresh write. Attempt 2 is a sentence repair when sentence_repair.plan() returns items, or a full rewrite when it returns None. Attempt 3 runs only when attempt 2's failures can all be fixed by sentence repair, and it never does a full rewrite. On a blog, attempt 3 first cuts F1/F9/F17 truth sentences that were already repaired once. It then repairs the rest, then deletes flagged sentences if that repair call fails, and otherwise falls back to attempt 2's text.

findings.claim: Code alone decides held vs approved. _hold_or_ship() holds on the first failed blocking gate that is not 'never_holds'. Gates in that class are F15_voice, F2_superlatives, F9_brand_style and the F14 under-floor block. After the loop, four more steps can still change the status. _cut_stock_lines and _enforce_authenticity cut sentences and re-derive the status. _final_integrity holds an approved piece on any F13_repeat residue. _degraded_final holds on a hard degraded marker: a judge outage, or a fallback writer when the stage's hold switch is on. 'Held' is a label only admins see. The tenant still receives the piece, but it cannot be published until it is edited or cleared.

findings.claim: F4_seo_surface needs a title of 45-60 chars, a meta of 120-158 chars ending in a full stop, the keyword in both, and a lowercase-kebab slug of at most 60 chars. These rules are deterministic, but an LLM is asked to meet them: _fit_seo_meta makes up to 2 t9_repair calls per attempt, then holds. The held reasons are almost all 'meta is 160-185 chars' or 'keyword missing', meaning the model miscounts characters. No code-side composer or truncation exists after the S232 cut was removed.

findings.claim: F9 is the T10 judge: one call per attempt, stage t10_judge, max_tokens 8192. It returns a blocking F9_cta_fact result and a warn-only F9_brand_style result. The live route lists gpt-5.6-luna@acc3, then gpt-6-luna@acc3, then gpt-6-luna-openai. acc3 refuses, so in practice every F9 verdict now comes from the third rung, gpt-6-luna-openai. In the week of 2 Nov, t10_judge logged 22 refused rungs against 72 answers. The same model judged 8 of 8 human-labelled 'pass' items as fail in R2 calibration run 858c8bf6. thresholds.yaml marks every pass line calibrated:false.

findings.claim: Each attempt runs a fixed chain of 12 deterministic edits on the blog before the gates read it, each wrapped in step_guard: ai_tells.rewrite, hygiene.autofix, ensure_cta, add_family_caveats, drop_restated_faq, drop_unanswerable_faq, drop_subjectless_faq, real_first_faq, fix_trip_facts, text_integrity.final_pass, length_trim. Only the FAQ regeneration among them calls an LLM. The edits can remove FAQ pairs, which then fails F16_faq. F16 cannot be repaired, so the only fixes are one regeneration for each fresh writer text plus one more per request after a repair ('faq_fell').

findings.claim: The AA-528 regression guard reverts a rewrite to the previous attempt when it newly fails a gate that used to pass and has no fewer blocking failures overall. Whether a piece ships therefore depends on the path it took. Two exceptions sit on top: AA-780 keeps a rewrite that followed an F14 floor block, and AA-1000 ignores failures that are only tier-2. Since F9 is an LLM verdict that varies from call to call, a revert can be triggered by judge noise rather than by text that got worse.

findings.claim: Only a process crash or interruption makes the t9_write job run again (max_attempts=2, concurrency=4). run_write_background turns every other exception into piece status 'failed' without re-raising. The exceptions it does re-raise are a budget-approval stop, the stage kill switch and an unreadable budget counter.

findings.claim: In the worst case, one blog makes about 38 LLM requests and 7 embedding calls. Doubling counts each one-shot budget or gateway truncation retry; gateway rungs that were refused for free are not counted. Breakdown: T8 = 2 angle calls x 2 = 4. In the job: FAQ filter 2; per attempt, writer or repair 2 + SEO fit 4 + judge 2, times 3 attempts = 24; FAQ regeneration at most 3 x 2 = 6 (attempt 1 fresh, attempt 2 full rewrite, one faq_fell); answer-fit 2. Each request can also walk a 3-4 model route. A crash re-run of the job doubles the job's part. The typical piece seen in the ledger uses about 8-12 requests.

systemic_problems: The first write almost never passes (4 of 187), so a blog's quality depends on the repair machinery rather than on the writer. Each failure mode added one more branch to the loop: 139 commits since 1 Sep, and a 750-line run_write_background. Fixes go in downstream, after the writer, instead of into the writer's contract.

Holds are decided by checks nobody has calibrated. The F9 LLM judge decides 34% of holds. It now runs on a third-choice fallback model (gpt-6-luna-openai, because acc3 refuses), and that model failed 8 of 8 human-labelled passes in R2. Every pass threshold says calibrated:false. Stored pipeline verdicts disagree with human labels on 10 of 31 golden items.

Deterministic constraints are handed to an LLM. The SEO title and meta character limits plus keyword coverage (F4_seo_surface) cause 23% of holds because the model miscounts characters, after 2 extra Haiku calls per attempt. FAQ pair counts are similar: code cuts pairs, then an LLM call puts pairs back.

The routing rules live in branch logic spread across files, not in one table. These all interact through ledger shapes, and every new gate needs edits in 3-5 places: sentence_repair._ELIGIBLE_GATES, CHEAP_REPAIR_GATES, OWNED_BY_FIX_STEP, STYLE_ONLY_GATES, never_holds, TRUTH_CUT_GATES, _cut_gates_repaired, the regression-guard exceptions and the merged-ledger expansion. taxonomy.yaml exists but does not drive this routing.

Outcomes depend on the path and on judge noise. The regression guard compares two LLM verdicts, the F9 sticky-pass memory papers over the judge contradicting itself, and the same text can be approved or held depending on which attempt was reverted to.

Shadow and off machinery adds code paths but no effect: t10_claims is routed but not wired, seed-align tier 1 and 2 are off with 0 calls, and F12 and F9_brand_style only warn. That is review and test surface on every change, with no measured benefit live.

Token and cost waste in the writer: a 12000 ceiling with adaptive thinking at effort high (now medium) gives p95 9487 output tokens for an article of about 1200 tokens. Cut replies are billed and discarded ($0.98 in 30 days on t9_write alone). Every t10_judge call first tries 2 acc3 rungs that are known to refuse.
proposals: Measure the stack before fixing it again. On the human-labelled blog set, compute precision and recall per gate (and per stage: writer, repair, cut). Demote any hold-capable gate below a precision bar to warn-only, F9_cta_fact first, until it is calibrated against labels. Record calibration.run_id in thresholds.yaml, which is the regression gate the tech lead asked for.

Make F4_seo_surface fully deterministic. Build the title and meta in code from the writer's candidates: trim at a clause boundary, insert the keyword, enforce the band and slugify. Or validate in code and accept only a candidate that passes, with no hold for character counts. That removes up to 4 t9_repair calls per attempt and 23% of holds.

Replace the branches in run_write_background with an explicit table-driven state machine: write → deterministic fixes → gates → per error class (from taxonomy.yaml: repair_sentence | cut | regenerate_section | rewrite | hold) → decide. Each gate's class in taxonomy.yaml should own its fixer and its hold rule. The 9 routing sets then collapse into one registry the lint checks.

Shift effort upstream to the writer. The pulled stats do not include attempt-1 failure frequencies per gate (gate_ledger_key), so collect them, then move the top 3 gate contracts into the writer's prompt and output schema. Run that through a writing-memory release with an A/B against release 0. The target is attempt-1 pass going from 2% to at least 50%, so repair becomes the exception.

Pin the F9 judge to one calibrated model with a route that puts the answering model first: drop the acc3 rungs while acc3 refuses, or reorder them. Log the verdict variance across attempts. Remove or wire t10_claims (claim_rules) and either delete or schedule the off seed-align tiers, so the code reflects what runs.

Cap writer tokens to the job: blog output ≤ about 6000 with effort medium or low, plus a structured body/meta schema. Alert on any t9_write row with stop=max_tokens (the route_cut alert exists in #1344), and track $/blog per attempt from llm_call_log.

Loop: attempt 1 = write → fit → edits → gates. Pass → approved. A non-repairable failure → held. Otherwise attempt 2 = sentence repair (plan() has items), SEO-only (plan() = [], no LLM call), or full rewrite (plan() = None), then the same chain. Attempt 3 only if plan(attempt 2) is not None, and it is repair or cut only. The regression guard can revert any attempt. After the loop: stock and authenticity cuts → tag strip → answer-fit → final integrity → degraded → store.

Worst case: about 38 LLM requests (T8 4 + filter 2 + 3 x [writer 2 + SEO 4 + judge 2] + FAQ 6 + fit 2) and 7 embeddings, times 2 if the job is re-run after a crash. Each request may walk a 3-4 model route.

systemic_problems: The same failure keeps coming back in different stages because each call site owns its own copy of a shared concern. Token ceilings were set separately in 6+ places (fixed 5 times before #1344). SEO length fits exist in S1 and again in T9 (5 + 9 fixes). Retry logic now runs in two layers (token_budget.py and the gateway).

There is no regression gate between a change and the live T9 blog. R2 has never produced a valid t9_blog verdict, the DB holds 1 human label on a blog, agent-panel noise (SD about 1.1) is about 7 times the ±0.15 bars, and live blog volume after 23/10 is 6 pieces. Prompt and gate rounds are therefore shipped or reverted on noise.

Families are fixed by adding gates or regex patterns rather than by changing what the writer receives. The gate count went from 9 to 26 live ids plus 4 retired. Families that converged (SEO, FAQ, F1) were fixed by code or by moving to a labelled LLM check. Families that keep failing (F17/F18, voice, embellishment) are still regex or prompt work.

The loop depends on repair: 0 of the last 49 approved blogs passed on attempt 1. Each new gate means more repair calls, and 20% of sentence repairs introduced a new blocking failure (S234). The integrity machinery then needed to guard those repairs grew to roughly 10k lines (hygiene, trip_facts, ai_tells, text_integrity).

Systemic fixes are built, then left off: seed alignment (T10_SA_MODE), the tier-2 adjudicator (T10_ADJ_MODE), F9 v2 claims (t10_claims), brief grounding and the reader checklist. Their routes are still kept up by migrations, but no production call ever reaches them.

Since #677 a held piece is still delivered to the tenant, so the gate verdict has no product consequence. Pass rates reported as 'PASS' measure delivery, which hides real gate holds (3 of 5 blogs held in the week of 11-02).
Gates were retired instead of fixed (F3, F5, F8, promises_an_option, F7 folded into F16). Their holds disappeared from the stats without any evidence that the writing improved.

Model swaps happen without a pre-flight check of the stages that depend on them. Moving to Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 / GPT-6 reopened truncation (and adaptive-thinking cost) in t9_write, t8, repair and faq_filter within a day. Every failure was already in the ledger, but no alert fired until route_cut was added in #1344.
proposals: Freeze new T9 prompt and gate rounds until a valid baseline exists. Run the S258 fixed 24-blog sample through the live T9 loop with the current route (Sonnet 5.5, effort medium, t9_write v2/v3). Record per-gate hold rates, attempt-1 pass rate, tokens_out p95 and cut count as baseline v1. Every later change to T9 must report against this baseline, with a repeat control arm in the same run.

Make the gate stack itself the first calibrated instrument, before any LLM judge. On the 18 frozen golden blogs, the pipeline verdict has a 40% false-pass rate (embellishment). Target that rate per failure class (fact.embellish, fact.misbinding, scope.framing) by running seed alignment in shadow (T10_SA_MODE=shadow, $0) and the adjudicator in shadow on the same 18 items. Promote a class to repair or hold only when its shadow precision is measured.

Decide the fate of the dead stages: either wire in F9 v2 (t10_claims) and the adjudicator, or delete their routes and code. Keeping them half-alive costs a migration every time routes change, and it hides that F17/F18 are still regex-only.

Make 'held' mean something again for measurement: report blog outcomes as gate-approved vs delivered in every audit, and track attempt-1 pass rate as the main KPI. A writer that needs repair on 100% of pieces is the failure to fix, not each gate it trips.

Collapse duplicated concerns into one owner: a single retry layer (keep the gateway's #1344 and make token_budget.py a thin caller), one SEO length-fit function shared by S1 and T9, and one length policy with a deterministic floor guard after every cut step (check the result against the 4,700-character F4 floor, not only the prompt).

Treat F10 cross-tenant duplication and topic supply as Slate problems. Measure F10 hits per tenant pair after #1342 on the 4 audit tenants, and add a 'subject already published by another tenant' check at Slate time instead of holding the written blog after a paid write.

Add a model-swap pre-flight: before a route migration changes a writer or judge model, run the contract smoke plus one real request per dependent stage, and compare tokens_out p95 and the cut rate against the stage's ceiling. Make route_cut (from #1344) a merge-blocking check in the migration PR, not only an e-mail.

Fix the stats script so gate_ledger and flags (presumably arrays) are counted per gate id. Then hold rate per gate can be tracked weekly against this fix list, as the regression signal for each family.

F18 trip_facts.py:636-720 blocks 'one of the most …' / 'nowhere else' unless the seed has a same-scope superlative. F9 v2 claim_rules.py:600-611 fails uncited background whenever the place has a card. systemic_problems: No single source of truth for content policy. Each layer (writer prompt, repair prompt, FAQ regen, FAQ filter, F9 judge prose, F9 v2 rule table, F17/F18 regexes, taxonomy definitions, eval judge rubric, golden label rubric, the written S223 policy) restates the policy in its own words. Fixes are made in one copy at a time, so the copies drift (the background, brief-as-source and reflection rows are the clearest cases).

The quality taxonomy lists only failures, never allowances. It has no 'allowed place background' or 'brief-supported' class, so any judge that reads the taxonomy (the eval judge) cannot apply the policy-A carve-out the writer was promised.

The golden set and eval rubric encode an older, looser policy (reflection = voice, brief = source) than the live writer and gates. Judge-to-label kappa therefore measures agreement with a different policy, and a 'better' judge can look worse.
Severity is defined twice: the taxonomy says warn while the gates block, and the reverse for scope. The Lab, the admin UI and the pipeline disagree on which defects matter.

Gates were added or retired without updating the prompt contract. The writer still gets the retired F3 rhythm rules, is not told the F17 timing or F18 rarity rules that block it, and is told a CTA style that ensure_cta overwrites.

Fixers and gates conflict with contracts: the FAQ filter keeps topics the dropper removes, F16 then holds, and the slug fixer creates a 'truncated' defect. The same pattern caused lessons.md:310 (S234), and it recurs because no test runs the whole chain on shared fixtures.
Parallel half-built policy engines (F9 v2 claim rules, seed-align tiers 1/2, t10_adjudicate) have active routes but 0 calls. Future fixes can land in a copy that never runs.

A fixed length floor (900 words) combined with tight seed-only rules makes thin seeds structurally unsatisfiable. The writer must pick which rule to break, and a different checker punishes each choice.
proposals: Write one machine-readable policy file (e.g. services/quality/policy.yaml). Give each topic an id (background, brief_source, reflection, timing, pace, rarity, numbers, scope, faq_topics, seo_bands, structure, cta) with allow/forbid text, examples and severity. Generate the matching paragraph of every prompt (writer, repair, FAQ regen, faq_filter, F9 judge, eval judge, label rubric) from it, and add a CI test that every prompt embeds the same rule ids and hashes. Prompt manifest bumps then follow automatically.

Get the tech lead to settle the open policy points once, as one decision page: (a) policy-A width: the S223 text including architecture/setting/'five-storey', or the narrower T9 text; (b) whether the brief and brand pack are a fact source; (c) whether reflection is voice or fact.embellish. Then align F18 (allow card-backed or policy-A superlatives of role), the F9 judge, the taxonomy (add allowance classes) and the eval rubric to that decision.
Relabel the T9 golden set under the settled policy before reading any more judge kappa. Until then, the AA-900 '0/8 pass labels' result is partly a label-policy mismatch, not only a judge defect.

Make the taxonomy the only source of gate severity: derive blocking from taxonomy severity and modes, and resolve the other.f7 / other.c3 / other.s5 vs F17/F16 and scope.framing vs F12 mismatches deliberately. Add the other.* classes the pipeline enforces to the eval judge, or score them with the same deterministic detectors inside the Lab.

FAQ chain: run drop_unanswerable_faq's topic test on the faq_filter KEEP list before the writer or regen sees it (deterministic, $0). Use one pair count (3-4 or 4) and one 'new vs restated' rule across writer, regen and dropper, and replace the faq_filter KEEP criteria that need numbers, travel times or 'what visitors usually do'.

Make the blog length floor scale with the seed (words per usable source fact, or a lower floor for thin or Segment-grain seeds), so the writer is never told to reach 900 words with material that later layers punish.

Bring the writer prompt in line with the gates it is judged by: add the F17 part-of-day/ordinal and F18 rarity rules, sharing the phrase lists with the regexes; drop or reinstate the retired F3 rhythm mandates; and state the CTA as its own literal sentence, as ensure_cta enforces.

Small deterministic fixes: cut the slug at a word boundary, make the writer meta band equal the gate band, and decide whether F1 should read spelled-out numbers (claim_rules.find_novel_word_numbers already exists) and exclude 'Other trips' lines as claim_rules does.
Delete or wire the dead layers (F9 v2 rules, t10_claims and t10_adjudicate routes) and record which one is the live fact policy, so no future fix targets a copy that never runs.

Add a cross-layer contradiction regression suite: about 10 fixed sentences per policy topic, labelled allowed or forbidden, run through every deterministic gate and fixer in CI ($0), plus a recorded-replay check of the judge prompts. A change that makes two layers disagree on a fixture fails the build. This turns the endless fix loop into a regression-gated one, in line with the standing direction.

systemic_problems: No funnel metric for the blog pipeline. Nothing records first-pass yield, held rate or attempts per approved blog per week, and nothing gates a release on them. The ~2% first-pass yield and the 53% held rate are visible only by hand-querying content_piece.

Cost cannot be attributed per piece or channel from the stage ledger. t9_write mixes full writes, rewrites and sentence repairs across 8 channels, so cost per approved or held blog is only an upper bound. The content_piece_id column exists but is not used in reporting.

held_reason keeps only the first failing gate in a fixed order. The stored gate_ledger is a JSON array that the aggregate queries missed. Gate-failure frequencies are therefore biased by order and incomplete, which is a weak base for taxonomy-driven tuning.

'Held' is an admin label only. Held blogs are delivered as ready, so the 3-attempt loop spends money on pieces it then ships with unresolved findings, including real invented tour promises (14 of the 34 F9 holds).

The gates and the judge are stricter than the written writer policy. About 14% of holds (F9 background-claim flags, F1 background numbers) fail content the source-fidelity policy explicitly allows. The policy is not encoded as a shared rubric for both writer and judge.

Mechanical defects (SEO length and keyword, slug, citation markers, duplicate CTA, FAQ count) are handled by gates plus LLM retries or fix rounds instead of a deterministic post-processor that guarantees the contract. They drove about 28-47% of holds and about 9 PRs in 3 days.

Model and route swaps (Sonnet 4.6 to 5.5 at effort high, judges acc3 to OpenAI to nova-lite) went live without a regression gate on live blogs. Result: a 36% cost leak on truncated t9_write calls, judges with kappa 0-0.14, and no measured live sample after the fixes because blog subjects ran out (Route grain).

Routes are configured for inert stages (t10_claims, t10_adjudicate, and t10_gates until 13/10), and the ledger has no 'error' rows. The pipeline as configured differs from the pipeline as run, and stage error rates cannot be observed.
proposals: Add a weekly blog funnel view, with a regression gate on any writer, judge or route change: created, approved, held, first-pass yield, attempts per approved, holds by every failing gate (unnest gate_ledger as jsonb_array_elements, not only held_reason), and $ per approved and held blog. Join llm_call_log.content_piece_id to content_piece.channel/status and group by quality_signal mode (write, rewrite, sentence_repair, seo_fit). This replaces the upper-bound method used here.

Make the mechanical contract deterministic and the final step before gating. A post-processor fixes the slug (already done), strips citation tags and duplicate CTAs, trims the meta at a sentence or clause boundary into 120-158 when possible (LLM SEO fit only when no boundary fits or the keyword is missing), and applies a code rule for F16 (ship with 1-2 valid FAQ pairs, or drop the FAQ section, instead of holding). F4/F16 holds should become impossible by construction. That covers about 28-47% of past holds.

Encode the writer source-fidelity policy as one rubric shared by the writer prompt, F1 and the F9 judge. Background facts about named places (history, geology, protected-area status) are allowed. Tour activities, services, times, views, and promises about pace or the group are not. Then re-score the 34 F9 and 4 F1 holds as a $0 replay (AA-918 f9_results path) to confirm that about 14 move to pass and the 14 invented-experience cases stay failed.

Decide what 'held' means for delivery. Either withhold or flag blogs held on product-truth gates (F9 invented experiences, F17, F18) from tenant publish, or stop spending attempt 3 on pieces that will ship anyway. Today 53% of Dev blogs ship with unresolved findings.
Treat F10 cross-tenant similarity on the same catalogue tour as a policy decision: warn, or force angle diversity at T8, instead of holding. It caused 2 of the 3 holds in the latest week.

Before phase 2, run one measured live slice: 1 tenant, blog only, about 10 pieces, about $2. Do it after #1341 (word band and floor), #1342 (Segment-grain slate) and migration 381 (effort medium), and record cut rate, tokens_out p95, first-pass yield and held families against this baseline: 2% first pass, 2.4 attempts per approved, 11.7% t9_write cut rate.

Grow human labels on real production blogs: 1 label exists today against 187 pieces and an 18-item calibration set. Without them no judge or gate change can be regression-gated; the production gate stack sits at kappa 0.34.
Write errors to the ledger as status='error', and remove or disable routes for unwired stages (t10_claims, t10_adjudicate), so that the pipeline as configured matches the pipeline as run.

findings.claim: There is a retry hole for the four stages that keep their own budget retry (t8_angle_gen, t9_write, t9_repair, t9_faq_filter). The gateway instead moves silently to the next route model (Sonnet 4.6 / Haiku 4.5). This is the main remaining reason for cuts and silent model swaps.

systemic_problems: Two owners of the truncation retry. Since #1344 the gateway owns the retry, but it is switched off for exactly the stages that cut most (t8, t9_write, t9_repair, t9_faq_filter). Their own retry only sees a cut reply that has text. An empty-content cut is classified as a generic unusable reply and becomes a silent move to an older model.

Thinking length is controlled per connection, not per model. Effort reaches the model only on the Anthropic Messages API; Converse (acc3) and OpenAI send nothing, so the same stage x model behaves differently depending on which deployment answered. The fix in migration 381 lapses when acc3 comes back.

Fallback chains mix model quality tiers (5.5 -> 4.6 -> GPT-6 -> nova-lite) for judges and validators with no mark, no hold and no eval. A route row that does not change while its answering rung does (acc3 refusals) is invisible to every gate.

Eval gating covers only part of the pipeline. The writing-memory release fingerprint covers t9_write's route row and the R2 judge's route row. It does not cover effort, ceilings, the five other blog LLM stages, the production F9 judge, or the model that actually answered. Model and effort changes go out through migrations with a manual 'read one paid blog' check.

The production judge and the eval judge are different routes and prompts, and both can drift to a different model or family on their own, so a 'pass' means different things over time. The R2 run that was meant to validate the judge ran on nova-lite, then on the model that failed calibration.
Ceilings are still per-call-site constants sized after each incident (more than 9 raises in about 4 weeks), not a budget derived from the observed p95/max of the stage x model x effort in the ledger.
proposals: Close the empty-cut hole in one place. Either let the gateway own the retry for all stages (drop budget_retry=False from token_budget and move the cut-row logging to the gateway's cut_reply_row with piece ids from the call scope), or classify BilledUnusableReply with stop_reason in TRUNCATED_STOP_REASONS as TRUNCATED so token_budget retries it. Add a regression test: an empty-content max_tokens reply on rung 0 must be retried on the same model at 2x before the route moves on.

Make effort a property of the stage x model on every way in. Send a reasoning control on Converse (additionalModelRequestFields once probed) and reasoning_effort on OpenAI. Until then, either pin t9_write to the Anthropic API deployment or have the route plan skip a deployment where the stage's effort row cannot be applied (fail closed rather than run at high).

Add a budget guard to CI and route_watch: for each stage x model, compare the ledger's 30-day out p95/max and reasoning p95 with the effective first ceiling (after stage_params and the floor). Alert when p95 is above 70% of the ceiling or the cut rate is above 2%. Today this flags t9_write (p95 0.79-0.99 of 12000) and the eval judge (p95 5626 against 4096).

Treat judge and validate fallbacks as degraded, like writer fallbacks. Mark the piece (degraded 'fallback_judge'/'fallback_validate'), and do not let nova-lite stand as the F9 or R2 judge: either drop nova-lite from the t10_judge and writing_memory_eval chains or make a nova-lite verdict count as 'judge unavailable' (the existing held path). Make R2 refuse a run whose judge model differs from the calibrated one.
Run the family rule in production too. Record the writer model on the piece (route_guard already knows it) and refuse or flag an F9 verdict from the same family.

Widen the reverify fingerprint to cover every blog stage in lab.py (t8, t9_write, t9_repair, t9_faq_filter, t9_faq_answer_fit, t10_judge), stage_model_params rows (effort), the effective ceilings, and the answering model mix from the ledger (the share of rung > 0 over the last N calls). A change to any of them sets reverify and blocks activation until an R2 run on the calibrated judge passes. Run reverify-scan automatically after a DB Migrate apply.

Re-validate the production F9 judge on gpt-6-luna-openai before trusting its holds. Re-run the 18-item calibration set with the F9 prompt (not the R2 prompt), at a fixed reasoning effort. If kappa stays below target, pin t10_judge to the last calibrated model or hold its verdicts as advisory.
Remove or mark the dead routes (t10_claims, t10_adjudicate while off) in the Lab stage list, so reviews and route checks do not treat them as part of the live pipeline.

Bound the whole write: give one piece an overall deadline (attempts x writer retry) and make the 24000-token retry respect the remaining connection timeout. Log latency per call so the 300 s timeout risk can be measured.

systemic_problems: No standing regression baseline. Each fix brings its own synthetic unit tests and a one-off replay script on a gitignored export. The next change never re-runs them, so the guard protecting fix N is not active when fix N+1 lands. About 144 blog-pipeline commits since 01/09 (61 to quality_gates.py, 98 to service.py, 37 to prompts.py); 5 commits ever touched the Q0 case files.

Enforcement does not match what fails. CI enforces only Q0 red-on-base for added cases, and the Q0 cases cover mechanical gates. The failure families that hold pieces (fact claims F1/F9/F17/F18/F12, SEO surface, FAQ count after droppers) have no corpus. The quality-paths map is report-only and misses about 30 blog files.

The paid end-to-end gate (R2) is structurally unable to pass for t9_blog: the judge is uncalibrated (best kappa 0.316 against a 0.6 bar), the cost is underestimated by about 2x, it covers the first draft only, and it runs by hand after deploy. So 'eval after deploy' never happened in practice for any blog change.

There is no ground truth. 1 human label among the 18 golden blog items and 1 human label on live blog pieces in 60 days. The agent-panel labels have kappa 0.40 against the human drafts, and the panel noise is larger than the effects being measured. Prompt rounds were accepted or reverted on noise.

The fingerprint and the change surface are disconnected. Route, effort / max_tokens and flag changes go live through migrations and env, and reverify sees only the t9_write route and the eval-judge route. Token-budget truncation recurred 4 times because no check compares cut rate per stage x model after a change, and the pre-v2 ledger recorded cuts as 'ok'.

Duplicate gate-input builders (PieceReplay, score.t9_gate_replay, plus several per-issue scripts) re-implement run_write_background with no parity test, so any replay may silently drift from production.

Volume gap: fixes landed while almost no blog pieces were being written (1 piece in the week of 26/10, 5 in the week of 02/11). Defects surfaced only in a later paid audit-tenant run (S271), not before merge.
proposals: L0 FREE, in CI, blocking: one canonical T9 replay harness. Promote scripts/quality/replay_aa924.py to tests/regression/t9_replay.py. Corpus: the 15 t9_blog + 15 LinkedIn samples of fixture-1.2.0 plus the audit-tenant blog pieces among the 187 stored in 60 days, deduped by seed hash, vendored as a versioned fixture (audit tenants only, no real tenant text). Store every attempt's text, ledger, repair_log and the stored LLM replies (F9 verdicts, FAQ filter / answer-fit verdicts, t9_repair patches) as cassettes. Each PR runs the full T10 + repair-routing + post-gate chain on base and head and diffs passed / held gate / per-sentence findings / repair plan per piece and mode. Any diff must be listed in a reviewed `expected_diffs.json` (same rule as q0-relabel). Cost $0, about 2 minutes CPU.

L0b FREE, post-deploy and post-migration: a read-only ledger health check per stage x model x connection over the last N calls after any deploy, route, stage_model_params or flag change. Fail when the cut rate (stop=max_tokens, truncated, billed_unusable) exceeds 2%, refused exceeds 5%, or tokens_out p95 is above 80% of the ceiling. This would have caught 12/10 (20 cuts at 2048), 22/10, 25/10 and 05-06/11 (7/68 t9_write, 7/44 t8).

Gate on per-class recall of BOTH labels: at least 6/8 pass-labelled items pass and at least 6/10 fail-labelled items fail, not only kappa. Fix the judge-source / source-fidelity policy mismatch first. Before that, get at least 10 human labels on blog items (the tech lead labels 20 stored pieces, $0), because 17/18 golden blog labels are agent-made.

L1 CENTS: replay the validate-role stages (FAQ filter, answer-fit, F9 fact) on stored inputs against the stored replies for model or route switches (for example the 04-05/11 move to haiku-5-5 / sonnet-5-5). Agreement must stay at or above a measured noise floor, below $0.50 a run.

L2 PAID, last and only for writer prompt / model / effort changes: R2 on the S258 fixed sample (at least 20 distinct blog inputs; create fixed-sample-v1.json first), running the FULL loop (gates + repair), not the first draft. Write the control twice (A and A') to measure writer noise, and set bars at ±2 SE instead of ±0.15. Correct R2_ITEM_ESTIMATE_USD t9_blog from 0.08 to about 0.17 and set the cap from the DRY RUN (about $4). Run it only after L0, L0b and L1 are green.

Process: the PR template's 'Quality' and 'LLM change' sections become CI-checked fields (a replay report ID or an R2 / L1 run ID, or an explicit `no-eval: <reason>` label), so a blog PR without evidence fails instead of merging empty. Each new lesson in the Pipeline and quality section must name the L0 case or check that enforces it before the lesson is closed.

recurring_families.family: 1. Output-token cuts and silent model swaps (t9_write, t8, t9_repair, faq_filter, eval judge)
recurring_families.root_cause: There is no single owner for the token budget. Ceilings are constants per call site, raised one incident at a time. Thinking length is controlled per connection, not per model: effort is sent only on the Anthropic Messages API, never on Converse (acc3) or OpenAI (client.py:2367, :2623). Two retry layers exist. VERIFIED today: token_budget sets budget_retry=False (token_budget.py:119-126), so the gateway retry is off for the four stages that cut most. token_budget itself only catches a cut reply that has text, or a TRUNCATED-classified error. An empty-content max_tokens reply (BilledUnusableReply, client.py:2569) is caught by the route's failed() (client.py:1683-1685), and the route moves silently to Sonnet 4.6 / Haiku 4.5. The gateway's own is_cut_failure (token_floor.py:146-154) would have retried it, but retry_allowed returns False (token_floor.py:122).
recurring_families.systemic_fix: Make one owner. Either the gateway owns every truncation retry (drop _own_retry, and log the cut row from the call scope), or token_budget treats an UnusableReply whose billed stop_reason is a cut as a cut. Add a regression test: an empty max_tokens reply on rung 0 is retried once on the same model at 2x before the route moves on. Add a static CI test that every route x stage_model_params row has a ceiling at or above token_floor(model, effort). Add a free post-deploy ledger check per stage x model x connection: cut rate over 2% or p95 over 70-80% of the ceiling fails it. Make effort fail closed: skip a deployment where the effort row cannot be applied.

plan.summary_vi:
Anh ơi, em đã soát lại toàn bộ khâu viết blog: từ chọn góc viết, viết bài, sửa câu, chạy các cổng kiểm, cho tới lúc bài được duyệt hay bị giữ.
Số liệu 60 ngày: 187 bài, giữ 99 bài (53%). Chỉ 4 bài qua ngay lần viết đầu, còn lại đều phải sửa thêm 1-2 lần.
Từ 19/10 tới nay chỉ có 6 bài blog chạy thật, nên hầu hết các bản sửa gần đây chưa từng được đo trên bài thật.
Sửa mãi không dứt vì ba lý do. Thứ nhất, cùng một luật về độ trung thực với nguồn được viết lại ở khoảng 10 chỗ (prompt viết, prompt sửa, bộ lọc FAQ, giám khảo, regex, bộ nhãn), mỗi chỗ một kiểu, sửa chỗ này thì lệch chỗ kia.
Thứ hai, không có lưới chống thoái lui: lần chạy chấm R2 nào cũng không hợp lệ, bộ nhãn blog chỉ có 1 nhãn do người gán, và mỗi bản sửa tự làm script kiểm riêng rồi bỏ.
Thứ ba, chỉ một lỗi là sửa cả vòng lặp sửa bài đã thành 750 dòng nhiều nhánh đặc biệt, và kết quả còn phụ thuộc vào độ dao động của giám khảo LLM.
Một lỗi mới em đã kiểm trong code: khi Sonnet 5.5 nghĩ hết trần token và trả về rỗng thì không được thử lại, mà âm thầm rơi xuống Sonnet 4.6.
Giám khảo F9 (chiếm 34% số bài bị giữ) từ 05/11 thực chất do model dự phòng thứ ba trả lời, chưa được hiệu chỉnh, và có thể rơi tiếp xuống nova-lite mà không ai biết.
Bài bị "giữ" vẫn giao cho đại lý ở trạng thái sẵn sàng, nên ba lần sửa tốn tiền nhưng không chặn được gì.
Kế hoạch em đề xuất đi từ rẻ đến đắt. Trước hết là đo đúng (sửa truy vấn thống kê), sửa lỗ hổng thử lại token, và dựng bộ chạy lại miễn phí trên bài đã lưu, chạy chặn trong CI.
Tiếp theo là các sửa bằng code: slug, dải độ dài meta, số cặp FAQ, CTA, sàn độ dài. Sau đó gom luật nguồn về một file chính sách duy nhất để sinh ra mọi prompt.
Anh cần chốt 3 điểm chính sách: bối cảnh về địa danh được rộng tới đâu, brief có được coi là nguồn hay không, và câu suy ngẫm tính là giọng văn hay là thêm thắt. Anh gán thêm khoảng 10-20 nhãn blog.
Lần chạy lại R2 đã duyệt nên làm sau các bước đó, chỉ chấm lại bài đã lưu (khoảng 6 cent), không viết lại bài (2,4 USD).
Chỉ bước sửa prompt viết là tốn tiền thật, khoảng 20-30 USD trên mẫu cố định, và cần anh đồng ý riêng.
Mục tiêu đo được: tỷ lệ bài qua ngay lần đầu tăng từ 2% lên ít nhất 30-50%, và mỗi thay đổi đều phải qua bộ chạy lại trước khi merge.
